From his command post at R2 in the heart of the Bois des Caures Colonel Driant had observed with affliction the fire of the flamethrowers flickering over his forward companies. Soon the enemy were closing in on the 'R-line', the line of concrete redoubts that contained R2. Eight hundred yards to the right, R1 had been taken from the rear by the Germans debouching out of the Bois de Ville, and at 1 p.m. they tried to rush R2 itself.

Rifle in hand, Driant took up an exposed position outside the redoubt, coolly directing and observing the fire of the Chasseurs around him. The air was thick with bullets, and when his men beseeched him to take cover he still stood there, remonstrating, 'You know very well they've never hit me yet!'

Bonus (from Wikipedia):

As the French defences crumbled all around them, Driant's two battalions â€“ 1,200 men in total â€“ began a desperate defence of the Bois des Caures in Flabas. Under his command, the battalions managed to resist the German onslaught until the afternoon of the next day, helping to gain the time that the French High Command needed to rush troops to the threatened sector. When his battalions were outflanked and the position was untenable, Driant ordered the survivors to withdraw. During the withdrawal, he was killed. He was regarded as a hero among the French at the time, and he and his men are still commemorated at a ceremony on 21 February every year.

He was buried initially by the Germans, who also wrote to his widow (via Switzerland) to assure her that he had been accorded full military honours. He was re-interred by the French where he fell in the Bois des Caures, where a memorial now stands to him and his men.

Source:

Horne, Alistair. "The Fall of Colonel Driant." The Price of Glory: Verdun 1916. New York: St. Martin's, 1963. 88. Print.

The Southern Forest had been left devastated in the wake of the Djinn's awakening. Countless trees had been uprooted by gale force winds, the ground fractured by innumerable earthquakes, waters fouled by mud and debris and a wall shattered in the Lost temple of Hom. Yet through all the destruction the splinter tribe of the Med'ja-Hom endured, spared by the blessing of a God and the kindness of new friends. The vine had been their savior, its supple creeping web binding the trees surrounding the tribe's encampment slowing their descent and providing a vital windbreak.

Though the Med'ja would lament the loss of their trees their death would feed the forest and reward them with a greater home in return.Beneath the Forest's surface fate had not been so kind to their compatriots.

The Chieftain's spirit had been shattered with the death of Me'le, his wife and partner among the council of Elders. Me'le, Grand Den Mother of the Med'ja-Hom and devotee to the Goddess Yuna had perished alongside many of her kin as the upper tunnels of the Med'ja's Great Burrow collapsed under the strain of the world's tremors. Those that survived now found themselves within the Burrow's lowest depths where soil gave way to stone.

Ma'Ten, Son of Dur'Ten, 9th Chieftain of the Med'ja-Hom and Lord of the Great Burrows sat, head hung, upon a boulder in a cave that had once served as a brewery, fragments of the once great vats and jars strewn upon the floor. Beside the Chieftain stood Ko'Da, Master Stonemason and last of the Council of Elders. "How severe was the damage?" The Chieftain asked without raising his head "I'm afraid it's quite extensive" The Elder replied, his hands twitching nervously "All major tunnels above the stone-line have suffered massive damage with many having collapsed entirely, below the stone-line there have been some fractures however I do not believe they pose a threat at this stage" "How long" Ma'Ten replied, his voice dry and hoarse "Weeks" Ko'Da replied "Assuming we receive assistance from the surface, we've lost many tools and even greater kin.

"No." The Chieftain growled, raising his head, his eyes were wet, surrounded by deep red rings and baring a gaze that could freeze the heart of even the strongest Holnareem warrior "My Lord?" The Elder queried, his eyes starting to water from the fumes that permeated throughout the cavern "NO!" The Chieftain roared striking the stone mason with the back of his hand "We will not lower ourselves to grovel at the feet of those who live above, we are the sons of Hom, masters of the earth, lords of stone and we will bow to no-one!" "But my lord!" The Elder begged "They are our brothers, our sisters, our allies!" "Where were they when the sons of nameless Gods marched into our home!? The Chieftain spat, kicking at his compatriot but striking only air "When we were at our most dire need they fled like children! They who would call our home, our birthright, an accursed place. No, they are no kin of ours"

Ko'Da rose to his feet shakily, a thin trail of blood dripping from his muzzle "But my lord, what shall we do?" The Chieftain turned to face the Elder his icy gaze focused somewhere beyond within the depths of the unknown "Our wells run deep and our mushrooms grow strong, we will endure. No longer shall we behold ourselves to those we once called kin, nor to the races that dwell above. The Med'ja-Hom shall dig deep, so deep that even the God's themselves shall not find us and when the weight of Ages comes crashing down and the light of Gaea shines its last we shall remain, undimmed before the breaking of the world...
